title: Hash-selector and structured witness finite-size comparison
status_note: Native backend components are implemented and development-checked. The measurement driver, frozen identities/protocol, checker, cost envelope and execution admission are not ready. No job is posted.
question: Do inverse-hash selector inputs and a structured witness backend lower full useful-relation cost against the current native hashed-base index-calculus baseline?
decision_value: A qualified reduction against the current native baseline would justify extending this finite-size backend while retaining the source-counting implementation. Equal or higher cost, especially on natural failed queries, would redirect the next implementation decision toward width-aware encodings or checked local recursion rather than repeating generic enumeration or SAT wrappers.

resources.notes: Unapproved placeholder envelope; not a measured cost estimate. Freeze a derived envelope after the native driver and exact workload exist.
